questions.q: State the principle of homogeneity of dimensions and explain why the equation v = u + at is dimensionally consistent while v = u + a is not, where v and u are velocities, a is acceleration, and t is time.
questions.a: The principle of homogeneity of dimensions states that in any physically valid equation, the dimensions of every term on both sides must be identical. For v = u + at: [v] = [L T⁻¹], [u] = [L T⁻¹], [at] = [L T⁻²][T] = [L T⁻¹] – all terms have dimension [L T⁻¹], so it is consistent. For v = u + a: [a] = [L T⁻²] which differs from [L T⁻¹], so it is dimensionally inconsistent. A wrong answer reveals the student cannot compute dimensions of derived quantities or does not understand that addition requires identical dimensions.

questions.q: A student writes the dimensional formula of Planck's constant h as [M L² T⁻¹] and claims that since angular momentum also has dimensions [M L² T⁻¹], they are the same physical quantity. Explain why this reasoning is flawed using the concept of dimensional analysis.
questions.a: Dimensional analysis only checks dimensional consistency, not physical equivalence. Two quantities having identical dimensions (like work and torque, both [M L² T⁻²]; or angular momentum and Planck's constant, both [M L² T⁻¹]) does not mean they represent the same physical concept. They differ in their physical definition, context, and tensorial nature (scalar vs vector vs pseudovector). A wrong answer reveals the student believes dimensional formula uniquely determines a physical quantity, confusing necessary condition with sufficient condition.

questions.q: The time period T of a gas bubble oscillating under water depends on pressure P, density ρ, and energy E of the explosion. Using dimensional analysis, derive the relation T ∝ P^a ρ^b E^c and find the values of a, b, c. Given: [P] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²], [ρ] = [M L⁻³], [E] = [M L² T⁻²].
questions.a: Assume T = k P^a ρ^b E^c. Dimensions: [T] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]^a [M L⁻³]^b [M L² T⁻²]^c = [M^(a+b+c) L^(-a-3b+2c) T^(-2a-2c)]. Equating powers: M: a+b+c=0; L: -a-3b+2c=0; T: -2a-2c=1 → a+c=-1/2. Solving: from T: c = -1/2 - a. Substitute in M: a+b-1/2-a=0 → b=1/2. Substitute in L: -a-3(1/2)+2(-1/2-a)=0 → -a-3/2-1-2a=0 → -3a=5/2 → a=-5/6. Then c = -1/2 + 5/6 = 1/3. So T ∝ P^(-5/6) ρ^(1/2) E^(1/3). A wrong answer reveals errors in setting up dimensional equations or solving simultaneous equations.

questions.q: The escape velocity v_e from a planet is given by v_e = √(2GM/R). A student proposes an alternative formula v_e = k G^x M^y R^z where k is dimensionless. Using dimensional analysis, determine whether this alternative form can be dimensionally correct and find x, y, z if possible. [G] = [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²], [M] = [M], [R] = [L].
questions.a: [v_e] = [L T⁻¹]. RHS dimensions: [G]^x [M]^y [R]^z = [M⁻ˣ L³ˣ T⁻²ˣ] [M^y] [L^z] = [M^(y-x) L^(3x+z) T^(-2x)]. Equating: M: y-x=0 → y=x; L: 3x+z=1; T: -2x=-1 → x=1/2. Then y=1/2, z=1-3/2=-1/2. So v_e = k G^(1/2) M^(1/2) R^(-1/2) = k √(GM/R). This IS dimensionally correct and matches the known form (with k=√2). The method works because we have three unknowns and three equations from M, L, T. A wrong answer reveals inability to handle fractional exponents or match dimensions of composite quantities like G.

questions.q: A physics textbook states: "The argument of a trigonometric function must be dimensionless." Evaluate the dimensional correctness of the equation x = A sin(ωt + φ) for simple harmonic motion, where x is displacement, A is amplitude, ω is angular frequency, t is time, and φ is phase constant. Justify your evaluation.
questions.a: The equation IS dimensionally correct. [x] = [L], [A] = [L] – LHS and first factor on RHS match. The argument (ωt + φ) must be dimensionless: [ω] = [T⁻¹], [t] = [T] → [ωt] = [T⁻¹][T] = [dimensionless]. [φ] is an angle (ratio of arc length to radius), so [φ] = [dimensionless]. Sum of two dimensionless quantities is dimensionless. sin(dimensionless) is dimensionless. Thus [A sin(...)] = [L] × [dimensionless] = [L], matching [x]. A wrong answer reveals the student does not recognize that angles and trigonometric arguments are dimensionless, or cannot verify nested dimensional consistency.

questions.q: Design a thought experiment to test whether the period of a simple pendulum depends on the mass of the bob using only dimensional analysis reasoning (no actual experiment). Explain what dimensional analysis predicts and what it cannot predict about this dependence.
questions.a: Dimensional analysis setup: T = k l^x g^y m^z. [T] = [L]^x [L T⁻²]^y [M]^z = [M^z L^(x+y) T^(-2y)]. Equating: M: z=0; L: x+y=0; T: -2y=1 → y=-1/2, x=1/2. So T = k √(l/g) m^0 = k √(l/g). Prediction: Period is INDEPENDENT of mass (z=0). What it CANNOT predict: The value of dimensionless constant k (which is 2π from actual dynamics). It also cannot rule out that T might depend on amplitude θ₀ if θ₀ is dimensionless (since dimensionless quantities don't affect dimensional equations). A poor answer reveals confusion between "dimensionally allowed" and "physically determined" dependencies.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Dimensional analysis is a mathematical technique used to check the dimensional consistency of physical equations and to derive ______ between physical quantities by expressing each quantity in terms of the seven base dimensions [M], [L], [T], [A], [K], [mol], [cd] and applying the principle of homogeneity of dimensions.
Fill in the blank: Observe a simple ______ in your school lab – a metal bob hanging from a string.
What is Dimensional analysis? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Dimensional analysis is a mathematical technique used to check the dimensional consistency of physical equations and to derive relationships between physical quantities by expressing each quantity in terms of the seven base dimensions [M], [L], [T], [A], [K], [mol], [cd] and applying the principle of homogeneity of dimensions.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Dimensional analysis?
questions.a: Students believe that if an equation is dimensionally correct, it is physically correct.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can independently verify the dimensional correctness of any given physics equation involving up to five physical quantities, and can derive the functional relationship between a dependent quantity and up to three independent quantities using the product-of-powers method, correctly identifying the exponents by equating dimensions.
